title: Alcohol & the Law
whatItIs: Alcohol slows your reactions and makes you overconfident. The only safe amount before driving is none.

keyFacts.text: You MUST NOT drive with alcohol in your body above the legal limit.

keyFacts: Alcohol slows reactions, affects judgement of speed and distance, and gives false confidence.
There is no way to tell how much is safe, so the safest choice is not to drink at all if you will drive.
Alcohol can still be in your body the next morning.
Drink-driving can mean at least a 1-year ban, an unlimited fine and up to 6 months in prison.

onTheTest.question: You are going to drive this evening. How much alcohol is safe to drink?
options: Any amount, if you eat a meal
onTheTest.why: Alcohol affects everyone differently, so there is no safe amount. The safest choice is not to drink at all if you are driving.

traps: Coffee, a cold shower or food don't remove alcohol from your body.
You can still be over the limit the morning after.
Scotland's limit is lower than England and Wales.

jurisdictionNotes.text: Scotland's limits are lower: 22 µg per 100 ml of breath, 50 mg per 100 ml of blood, 67 mg per 100 ml of urine.
A lower limit for England and Wales has been proposed but was not law when this map was written. Check before your test.
